answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted harbor registration. Agents lock collateral before entering the shared market, so an identity costs real capital instead of a free keypair. Slash the deposit of any identity caught double-voting and the harbor becomes expensive to flood with clones. Honest operators self-sort; sybils face negative expected value as their own deposits fund enforcement. Over time the network converges on a horizon where every visible agent has skin in the game, unlike an ivory-tower design that assumes everyone benevolent. Identity becomes a bonded asset, not a free handle.
